To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reaction of a ruthenium complex with the carbon-carbon triple bond of 3-alkyn-1-ol results in the formation of a ruthenacyclopentadienone, and that this complex reacts further with an aldehyde to yield an α,β-unsaturated ketone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of functionalized organic molecules from readily available starting materials.
the development of new methods to synthesize functional organic molecules via cleavage of C–C bonds.
the development of new catalytic methods for the synthesis of functional organic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ruthenium-cyclopentadienyl complexes are highly versatile catalysts for the cleavage and reconstruction of carbon-carbon bonds.
the Ru-catalyzed cleavage of C–C bonds in the presence of nucleophiles and/or electrophiles is a very powerful tool for the synthesis of functional molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ruthenium-cyclometallated complex is a good catalyst for the cleavage of the carbon–carbon bonds in various organic molecules.
ruthenium catalyzed carbon–carbon cleavage reactions are very useful tools to construct functional organic molecules.
we have developed a new method to synthesize functionalized organic molecules from the cleavage of carbon-carbon bonds using ruthenium complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ruthenium catalyzes the cleavage of the C–C bond, but it is not necessary to use a ruthenium catalyst for the synthesis of functional molecules.
the use of a catalyst can be used to control which carbon–carbon bonds are cleaved in the presence of a mixture of carbon–carbon bonds.
the use of the ruthenium catalysts in the synthesis of complex molecules is very effective, as it is not only the carbon–carbon bonds that are broken, but the entire molecule is also reconstructed.
